statement:
I turn everyday moments, thoughts and feelings into art.
Ordinary life, hand-painted, finished in gold and silver leaf.
shortBio: Contemporary artist working from a small, bright studio. Handmade pieces with expressive strokes and gold and silver leaf, each one drawn from a real moment.

seoTitle: Samridhi Agarwal | Contemporary artist, everyday moments in gold and silver leaf
seoDescription: Handmade contemporary art drawn from everyday moments, thoughts and feelings. Original pieces, gifting for Diwali, weddings and new homes, and commissions. Ships across India and worldwide.

footerFaqs.q: How do I care for a piece with gold or silver leaf?
footerFaqs.a: Keep it out of direct sunlight and away from damp walls. Dust gently with a dry, soft cloth. Never use water or spray cleaners on the surface.
Canvases arrive with finished, painted edges and can hang as they are. If you would like a float frame in oak, walnut or black, ask when you enquire and I will quote it.

Within India, pieces are packed in a custom box and shipped insured, usually within 5 to 7 working days. International orders go via Etsy or DHL; allow 2 to 3 weeks and note that import duties are the buyer's responsibility.
If a piece arrives damaged, send photos within 48 hours and I will replace or refund it. Because each piece is handmade, I don't otherwise accept returns, so please ask any questions before you buy.

title: The story behind Chai at Six
excerpt: A dark kitchen, one flame, and the steam that I chased with silver leaf for two weeks.

cover.alt: Steam rising from a chai pan in a dark kitchen

children.text: My mother wakes up at half past five. By six the chai is on and the kitchen is dark except for the blue flame and the steam. For years I walked past this. Then one morning I sat on the counter and watched.

The steam was the hard part. Paint made it look solid. Ink made it look like smoke. Silver leaf, torn into thin strips and pressed on almost dry, finally did it: it disappears and reappears as you move around the room, exactly like the real thing did when the light came in.
What I kept, what I left out

There is no pan, no cup, no stove in the painting. Just the grey of the room and the line of silver rising. If you know the moment you will see it. If you don't, I hope it still feels like the start of a day.

title: Forty-one diyas, counted twice
excerpt: Why Diya Count is exactly 120 cm wide, and why there are always forty-one marks.

cover.alt: A row of brass diyas on a parapet at dusk

children.text: Our parapet is a little over a metre long. Every Diwali the diyas go along it in one row, and every year my father counts them twice. It is forty-one. It has been forty-one since I was ten.

So the canvas is 120 cm wide, roughly the parapet, and the marks are gold leaf pressed on with my thumb. A few are copper leaf, for the ones that always go out first. This was the first piece where I let the surface stay rough, and I think that is why people want to touch it.

title: Two threads, two cities
excerpt: Tying a rakhi over a video call, and the small painting that came out of it.

cover.alt: A rakhi thread on a wooden table beside a phone

children.text: My sister is in Dubai now. On Raksha Bandhan she ties a rakhi on her own wrist while I tie one on mine, both of us on a video call, both of us pretending it is the same thread.
Two Threads is small on purpose. It had to fit in the hand luggage when I flew to see her. Gold on her side, terracotta on mine, and they cross in the middle where the call connects.

heading: Ordinary days, gold and silver leaf
intro: I am Samridhi. I paint the moments most people walk past: chai at six, a doorbell at nine, a list on the fridge. Each piece starts as a note on my phone and ends as a canvas with real gold or silver leaf, so the light in your home finishes it.

process.title: Notice
process.text: A moment catches me. I write one line about it, usually on my phone, before it fades.

process.title: Sit with it
process.text: Some notes wait months. When one keeps coming back, I know it wants to be painted.

process.title: Build the surface
process.text: Gesso, modelling paste, layers of acrylic. I work on the floor and let the strokes stay visible.

process.title: Leaf
process.text: Gold or silver leaf is laid on last, by hand, then sealed. It is the part that changes with your light.

exampleMoment: The morning of my cousin's wedding, someone dropped a whole basket of marigolds on the stairs and nobody minded. The stairs, the shoes, the sari hems, everything went orange. I wrote 'marigolds on the stairs, nobody minded' and six weeks later it became Marigold Morning.

heading: A piece about your moment
intro: Most of my commissions start with a sentence: the day we got the keys, our first monsoon in this flat, my father's chair. Tell me the moment and I will paint it.

steps.title: Tell me the moment
steps.text: Fill in the form below. The more ordinary the moment, the better it usually paints.

steps.title: We talk
steps.text: A short call or WhatsApp chat about size, colours, budget and where the piece will hang. I send a written quote and a mood sketch.

steps.title: Deposit and start
steps.text: A 50% deposit books your slot. I share two or three progress photos so you see it grow.

steps.title: Leaf, seal, ship
steps.text: Gold or silver leaf goes on last. Once it is sealed and dry I pack it in a custom box and send tracking.

whatToShare: Wall size, or the size you are imagining
A photo or two of the space
Colours you love and colours you do not
The moment, thought or feeling to capture
The occasion, if there is one
Any deadline, like a wedding or a housewarming
typicalTimeline: Most commissions take 4 to 6 weeks from deposit to delivery. For festival or wedding dates, please get in touch at least 8 weeks ahead.
priceGuide: Commissioned pieces start at ₹18,000 for a 30 x 40 cm canvas and ₹60,000 for 75 x 100 cm. Gold leaf adds roughly 10 to 15 per cent.
